subject: Brightline: urgent production degradation — exec bridge and RCA delivery
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightline.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Support <support@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-10-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Production: spike in latency + 5xx errors — need exec bridge

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a steep latency increase around 07:45 PT this morning across our inference endpoints. Error rate (5xx) rose from ~0.3% to 12% and median P95 latency jumped from 90ms to ~1.2s. The surge correlates with a high request volume on model-edu-v2 (seq len ~1024) but we also saw KV cache misses. Our SLOs are failing and some critical user flows are blocked.

Can we get an executive-bridge now? We need:
- immediate mitigation plan and ETA to stabilize
- root cause hypothesis and evidence (logs/traces)
- timeline for fixes and owner for each action item

Attaching a brief logs snippet from our side (small sample). Please escalate — this is impacting a key demo this morning.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen\Customer Success Lead\Brightline AI

Attachments: brightline_request_sample.log (text, 48KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightline.ai>
Cc: Brightline Support <support@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-10-15T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: spike in latency + 5xx errors — need exec bridge

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and sample logs. I'm setting up an exec bridge for 08:45 PT and pulling the relevant traces and KV cache metrics now.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- 08:45 PT bridge (dial-in to follow)
- I will attach the initial server traces and a short mitigation checklist during the bridge
- If appropriate, we can enable temporary throttling for non-critical routes to protect the demo endpoints

I'll loop in our on-call owners and our latency lead. Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize Brightline.

—Olga
Principal Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-15T08:35:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production: spike in latency + 5xx errors — immediate exec bridge & ownership

Team — forwarding Brightline's escalation. Bridge scheduled 08:45 PT. Quick asks before bridge:
- Jonas: pull GPU kernel metrics, shard utilization, and recent kernel selection logs for model-edu-v2 back 2 hours
- Ben: check KV cache eviction rate and prefix cache hit ratios; share top 50 keys with misses
- Kim: confirm whether any recent rollout/quantization/optimization hit Brightline's model versions in the last 48 hours

Bring an initial mitigations slide (2–3 bullets) for the bridge. We need a we-can/do-now plan + owners for immediate actions.

If you can't make the bridge, flag now and @marissa_cole will cover.

—Olga
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-15T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: spike in latency + 5xx errors — immediate exec bridge & ownership

I pulled the kernel and shard metrics. Interim findings:
- Two GPU hosts showed sustained context-switching and elevated kernel queue lengths starting ~07:40 PT; observed mismatch in kernel selection that increased token time for long sequences.
- KV cache eviction increased due to an unexpected workload pattern that bypassed prefix caching (high cardinality prefixes).

Immediate mitigations I propose for the bridge:
- Evict problematic hosts from the routing pool (roll traffic to healthy shards) — Ben to coordinate routing change
- Apply aggressive small-batch scheduling for model-edu-v2 to reduce kernel queueing (10–15min window)
- Enable short-lived read-through from cold storage for top-failure keys to avoid catastrophic misses

I'll bring the metrics to the bridge and volunteer to own the interim routing change.

—Jonas
Senior SRE
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightline.ai>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@brightline.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-16T14:05:00Z
Subject: Brightline — post-incident RCA & action tracker (initial delivery)

Sara / Kevin — thank you for the bridge yesterday and for your patience. Attached is the initial RCA packet and an action tracker with owners and target dates. Summary:

What happened (summary):
- A sudden workload pattern with high-cardinality prefixes caused KV cache miss amplification while two GPU hosts experienced kernel selection path regressions under long-sequence loads. The combination produced higher P95 latency and a spike in 5xx responses during a traffic burst.

Evidence included in packet:
- Timeline and traces (SPAN IDs) showing onset and recovery windows
- Kernel selection logs and GPU queue length graphs
- Sample error traces and correlation to KV miss events

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Re-routed traffic away from two affected hosts (08:55 PT)
- Temporarily applied small-batch scheduling for model-edu-v2 (09:05–09:20 PT)
- Prefilled top 200 hot keys into prefix cache for Brightline (09:10 PT)

Open corrective actions (owners + targets):
- Fix kernel selection regression in runtime (Jonas) — target: 2027-11-05
- Improve prefix caching heuristics & add adaptive eviction guard (Ben) — target: 2027-10-28
- Add automatic surge-detection alert and routing playbook (Kim) — target: 2027-10-22
- Follow-up runbook review with Brightline and validation window (Olga) — target: 2027-10-20

Attachments: brightline_rca_v1.pdf, kvcache-error-snippets.tar.gz, action_tracker_sheet.csv

Please review and let me know if you want us to move any target earlier. We propose a brief review call on 2027-10-18 to validate closures for the first two action items.

—Olga
Principal Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightline.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@brightline.ai>, Brightline Support <support@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-10-18T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Brightline — post-incident RCA & action tracker (initial delivery)

Olga — thank you for the thorough packet, and thanks to the ops team for rapid mitigation. The RCA is clear and the evidence aligns with what we see on our side. Two asks before we close this:

1) Can Jonas and Ben provide a short (10–15m) run-through of the kernel-fix plan and the adaptive cache changes on the 2027-10-20 validation call?
2) We need a target date for a production QA window where Brightline can run high-cardinality tests at scale; please propose a slot by EOD 2027-10-19.

If we get agreement on the above, Brightline will sign off on the RCA and track the action items in your shared tracker.

Best,
Sara
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-10-18T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Brightline — post-incident RCA & action tracker (initial delivery) — internal confirmation

Quick internal note:
- Jonas and Ben: please confirm availability for the 2027-10-20 10:00 PT validation call and prepare the 10–15m technical walkthroughs Sara requested.
- Kim: prioritize the surge-detection alert and share a draft playbook by EOD 2027-10-19 to meet Brightline's requested QA slot.

I'll update the tracker with agreed dates and send a calendar invite once we confirm. Thanks team.

—Olga
